MODEL EVALUATION¶

In [6]:
import numpy as np
import joblib
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
from sklearn.metrics import (
    confusion_matrix,
    classification_report,
    roc_auc_score,
    f1_score,
    precision_score,
    recall_score,
    log_loss
)
import time  # Import the time module

def evaluate_model(model, test_sets, true_labels_list, threshold=0.5):
    plt.figure(figsize=(12, 10))

    # Initialize lists to store metrics for averaging later
    roc_auc_list = []
    f1_list = []
    precision_list = []
    recall_list = []
    log_loss_list = []
    prediction_times = []  # List to store prediction times

    for i, (test_data, true_labels) in enumerate(zip(test_sets, true_labels_list)):
        # Start time for predictions
        start_time = time.time()
        
        # Predict probabilities on the test data
        probabilities = model.predict_proba(test_data)[:, 1]  # Get probabilities of the positive class
        predictions = (probabilities >= threshold).astype(int)  # Convert probabilities to binary predictions
        
        # End time for predictions
        end_time = time.time()
        prediction_time = end_time - start_time
        prediction_times.append(prediction_time)  # Store the prediction time
        
        # Calculate metrics
        roc_auc = roc_auc_score(true_labels, probabilities)
        f1 = f1_score(true_labels, predictions, average='weighted')
        precision = precision_score(true_labels, predictions, average='weighted')
        recall = recall_score(true_labels, predictions, average='weighted')
        log_loss_value = log_loss(true_labels, probabilities)
        
        # Store metrics for averaging
        roc_auc_list.append(roc_auc)
        f1_list.append(f1)
        precision_list.append(precision)
        recall_list.append(recall)
        log_loss_list.append(log_loss_value)

        # Print metrics for each test set
        print(f"Results for test set {i + 1}:")
        print(f"Prediction Time: {prediction_time:.4f} seconds")
        print(f"ROC AUC Score: {roc_auc:.4f}")
        print(f"F1 Score: {f1:.4f}")
        print(f"Precision: {precision:.4f}")
        print(f"Recall: {recall:.4f}")
        print(f"Log Loss: {log_loss_value:.4f}\n")
        
        # Confusion matrix
        cm = confusion_matrix(true_labels, predictions)
        
        # Classification report
        report = classification_report(true_labels, predictions)
        print("Classification Report:\n", report)
        
        # Plot confusion matrix
        plt.subplot(2, 2, i + 1)
        sns.heatmap(cm, annot=True, fmt='d', cmap='Blues')
        plt.title(f'Confusion Matrix for Test Set {i + 1}')
        plt.xlabel('Predicted Labels')
        plt.ylabel('True Labels')

    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()
    
    # Calculate and print average metrics
    print("Average Metrics Across All Test Sets:")
    print(f"Average ROC AUC Score: {np.mean(roc_auc_list):.4f}")
    print(f"Average F1 Score: {np.mean(f1_list):.4f}")
    print(f"Average Precision: {np.mean(precision_list):.4f}")
    print(f"Average Recall: {np.mean(recall_list):.4f}")
    print(f"Average Log Loss: {np.mean(log_loss_list):.4f}")
    print(f"Average Prediction Time: {np.mean(prediction_times):.4f} seconds")




test_sets = [test_1, test_2, test_3, test_4]
true_labels_list = [labels1, labels2, labels3, labels4]

NOTE:¶

--> 0 is class "BAD" and 1 is class "GOOD"¶

--> Time taken : Inference time taken by model to predict on 1000 images (Feature extraction and Image preprocessing is not included only model prediction time)¶

SPEED TEST FOR IMAGE PRE-PROCESSING and FEATURE EXTRACTION¶

In [13]:
import numpy as np
import tensorflow as tf
from tensorflow.keras.applications import DenseNet121
from tensorflow.keras.models import Model
from tensorflow.keras.layers import GlobalAveragePooling2D
from PIL import Image
import cv2
import time
import random

def build_densenet_feature_extractor(input_shape=(224, 224, 3)):
    base_model = DenseNet121(weights='imagenet', include_top=False, input_shape=input_shape)
    x = GlobalAveragePooling2D()(base_model.output)
    model = Model(inputs=base_model.input, outputs=x)
    return model
model = build_densenet_feature_extractor()

def preprocess(img_path):
    img = Image.open(img_path)
    img = np.array(img)
    img = cv2.resize(img, (224, 224))
    img = tf.keras.applications.densenet.preprocess_input(img)
    img = np.expand_dims(img, axis=0)
    return img

def feature_extraction(img_path):
    img = preprocess(img_path)
    features = model.predict(img, verbose=False)
    return features

def evaluate_feature_extraction_times(image_paths, num_iterations=10):
    preprocessing_times = []
    feature_extraction_times = []
    combined_times = []

    for _ in tqdm(range(num_iterations)):
        for img_path in random.sample(good_images,1):
            # Time preprocessing
            start_time = time.time()
            img = preprocess(img_path)
            end_time = time.time()
            preprocessing_times.append(end_time - start_time)

            # Time feature extraction
            start_time = time.time()
            features = model.predict(img, verbose=False)
            end_time = time.time()
            feature_extraction_times.append(end_time - start_time)

            # Time combined process
            start_time = time.time()
            features_combined = feature_extraction(img_path)
            end_time = time.time()
            combined_times.append(end_time - start_time)

    avg_preprocessing_time = np.mean(preprocessing_times)
    avg_feature_extraction_time = np.mean(feature_extraction_times)
    avg_combined_time = np.mean(combined_times)

    print(f"Average Time for Preprocessing: {avg_preprocessing_time:.4f} seconds")
    print(f"Average Time for Feature Extraction: {avg_feature_extraction_time:.4f} seconds")
    print(f"Average Time for Combined Process: {avg_combined_time:.4f} seconds")

OBSERVATION:¶
    

  • These 3 models  SVC with PCA, LightGBM and CATBOOST are top performing models with average accuracies of 85.5% for SVC, 85.3% for LightGBM and 85.7% for CATBOOST
    • 

  • But SVC is SLOWEST among the models with 4.3 Sec for prediction of 1000 images. And CATBOOST took only 0.057 Sec for And LightGBM took 0.02 Sec only.
    • 

  • The fastest model is LDA with speed 0.003 Sec and Accuracy 83.26%
    • 











CONCLUSION¶
    

  • CATBOOST and LightGBM are two best choices to consider which offers good speeds and very good accuracies. CATBOOST is slightly slower but more accurate where as LightGBM is slightly faster but less accurate.
    • 

  • I would suggest CATBOOST is best, since these speeds were for 1000 images. For a single image it will be in Micro seconds (1e-6), which is almost negligible and kind of similar for both models. In that case CATBOOST is clearly better than LightGBM
    •
